newsitem.title: USA: More Americans file jobless claims last week.
newsitem.headline: More Americans file jobless claims last week.

text.p: The number of people filing for first-time unemployment benefits jumped by 25,000 last week as claims activity picked up from a 23-year low recorded the week earlier, the Labour Department reported on Thursday.
Despite the rebound, claims for the week ended Aug. 2 were still at the relatively low level of 300,000. Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected initial claims for last week to rise to 307,000.
The department said its four-week average of initial claims stood at the lowest level since the week ended Feb. 25, 1989.
Many economists view the moving average as a better indicator of labour trends than the more-volatile one-week figures.

The average fell to 303,750 last week from 325,250 the previous week. The figure includes data for the week ended July 26, when claims fell to 275,000, the lowest level since the week ended Jan. 5, 1974, when they stood at 269,000.
The total number of Americans continuing to collect benefits rose by 32,000 to 2,352,000 in the week ended July 26, the latest period for which the data were available.
The department said 12 states and Puerto Rico reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended July 26, the latest period for which the data were available.

Among the largest states were Tennessee, with 10,142 fewer initial claims, North Carolina, down 8,363, Alabama off 6,045, Michigan down 5,225, California with 3,902 fewer claims, Missouri, off 3,759, and South Carolina, down 3,555.
Tennessee said it had fewer layoffs in a wide range of industries, some of which included construction, service, apparel and electronic equipment.
North Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the textile, apparel, furniture and non-electrical machinery industries.

Alabama had fewer layoffs in the textile, apparel, lumber and electrical machinery industries. Michigan reported fewer layoffs in the automobile industry, while California said it had fewer layoffs in agriculture.
Missouri said it had fewer layoffs in the transportation industry, while South Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the textile industry.

Indiana was the only state to report an increase in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the July 26 week, the department said. It reported 4,774 additional claims, due mainly to layoffs in the transportation equipment and primary metals industries.
